Content: Delivery Specialist checking in! Dirk's task is to draft congratulatory letters to winners of Lily's Choice Award. His goal is to motivate them to take action (respond to his message and accept the award) to prepare for their internship. Dirk should also use a formal and friendly tone, and he should be sure to lay everything out in a straightforward way that does not overwhelm the reader with too much unnecessary information. He should make his best attempt to not leave any important questions unanswered, but still add a good-will ending with contact information in case of questions. To motivate the recipients, Dirk should be sure to describe the ways in which accepting this award and participating in the internship will benefit them, such as the potential to earn a higher income and distinguishing themselves from other students. Dirk should type this letter but have Lily sign it in her handwriting.

The relationship between Lilian and Dirk shows a power dynamic. Lilian gives direction to Dirk but sometimes limited detail leaving Dirk the responsibility to interpret expectations, be on time, and take care of follow-ups. Dirk is expected to balance quality and efficiency, the letter must be made using the notes given by Lilian. The tone and the professionalism of the letters is rather important. Rhetorical Delivery Strategy In this rhetorical situation, it is my responsibility as the Delivery Specialist to select the most effective communication channel, tone, timing, and structure. Based on our discussion and research, my group would send the award notification messages in a manner consistent with the audience, the urgency of the issue, and the organization's expectations. Notifying Lily’s Choice Award recipients is Dirk's responsibility, but he must do so promptly, professionally, and with limited power. Effective corporate communication requires the harmonious operation of the audience, purpose, timing, tone, medium, and rhetorical contexts, as emphasized throughout corporate Communication. In this instance, choosing a communication method that aligns with Lilian Fung's brand and listeners' capacity to respond is more important to the message's effectiveness than crafting exquisite language. The distribution method was consistently selected by the panel as the most important consideration. Since Lilian demands efficiency and speed, an email is required to ensure that recipients receive the information right away. However, some group members noted that the significance and gravity of the prize could not be adequately communicated by email alone. The committee decided that an email and a formal printed letter would be the two synchronized channels for sharing the information to strike a balance between professionalism and urgency. While the physical letter reiterates authenticity, value, and brand trust, the email guarantees an instant connection. One of the main topics of debate in the group was tone. Even though the message needs to be professional, fashion students would probably be turned off by an overly official or businesslike tone. Rather, the committee decided that the tone should be one of encouragement, warmth, and congratulations, akin to the success and joy that are highlighted in college acceptance letters. Lilian's actions convey a feeling of urgency and a commitment to fulfilling deadlines. The committee decided that delivery should take place early in the week because sending the message late on a Friday may cause it to be missed or delayed. It is more likely that recipients will get the email and reply within the anticipated time if the letter and email are coordinated at this point. The committee carefully considered the structure and clarity of the format. Following the announcement of the winner as the recipient of an award, the correspondence should provide clear instructions on how to proceed with the internship opportunity and what the incentive entails. The panel concluded that stressing exclusivity without providing precise numbers would maintain the award's perceived excellence and keep it from losing its significance, despite disagreements about whether to reveal the number of nominees. Finally, the group agreed to arrange for further correspondence. Given the high stakes and urgency of the time, one message might not be sufficient. Sending a follow-up email if no answer is received will demonstrate professionalism, ensure accountability, assist Lilian in achieving her goals, and provide the recipients with the confidence to respond. Hey all, Role: Message Designer For this situation, Dirk is an administrative assistant ready to help his boss Lilian Fung draft up some letters to write to 3 up and coming fashion designers in college. This year they got 25 applicants and chose 3 for to win the Lily's Choice Awards. This comes with a cash prize as well as an internship with the Lilian Fung Collection. This message is not only important for the receiver of it, but also the sender. Just like any other internship, getting people that are good at the job they do and getting them interested in your company are very important! Dirk needs to draft these messages as not only congratulatory, but he needs to sell them on coming to Lilian Fung Collection for their internship. At the start of his messages, he should be very congratulatory. This is a great honor and telling them this will make them very happy to have won. Dirk needs to emphasize the selectiveness in this award. Explaining that out of all of the applicants (25) that applied, these people were chosen specifically because of how good their work was. This will make the message feel more personal and that Lily chose them for a reason. Dirk can then explain how important an internship is and why Lilian Fung Collection is the right place for them to apply their skill learned in college and learn something that will help kick start their careers. At the end of the letter, Dirk should re-emphasize the congratulatory response of winning the award and confidently remind them that this is a fantastic opportunity that they need to call in to action. Mentioning the timeline of the banquet and getting them to sign the internship is critical. Dirk should end the letter with excitement to meet them and hopefully helping them at Lilian Fung in the very near future. Thank you! Let me know if you guys have questions. Mike Helsel

Part 1: CAST Analysis Context The Lilian Fung Collection is informing a student that he or she has been chosen as the winner of the Lily Choice Award. This prize will include a cash prize of 1000 dollars, a commemoration plaque and a 6-month paid internship in Toronto. Awards will be given on May 7, between 6:00 and 8:00 p.m. in the Bistro of Fondini on the West Campus. The recipient has to confirm attendance and contact the firm to make arrangements for the internship. Audience The targeted reader is a fashion design student in fourth year and in the early stage of the career. Strategy The format used will be a direct positive message: a congratulations opening, stating the award clearly, including definite design feedback, providing the banquet information, giving an idea of what to do in case of not being able to attend, giving instructions to address the internship coordinator and a closing encouraging note. Tone It will be professional, warm, enthusiastic, and yet straightforward and educational. Part 2: Congratulations Letter Lilian Fung Collection, Inc. Toronto, ON Rashana Develani Apt. 807, 439 High Tech Rd Richmond Hill, ON Dear Ms. Develani, It is my pleasure to inform you, on behalf of the Lilian Fung Collection, that you are one of the winners of this year's Lily Choice Award, which honors the innovative contributions in the field of women's fashion design. Ms. Fung found the elaborate use of beading to bring a higher class to a casual weekender shape impressive. The contrast between the fabrics of a texturally rich nature made a strong visual impression, which, at the same time, testified to the uniqueness of the creative process and the solid knowledge of the technical skills. The new thinking and attention to detail that the collection is looking for in the new designers is reflected in your work. To commend your success, Lily’s Choice Award would grant you a financial grant of 1,000 dollars, a commemorative plaque and a six month, paid internship in the Toronto studio of the Lilian Fung Collection. The acceptance will be held in your institution's awards banquet on May 7, between 6:00 and 8:00PM, at the bistro of Fondini, West Campus, 211 Spadina Rd. One of the Lilian Fung Collection members will be present. In case you are not available, please take time to notify us as soon as possible so that other arrangements can be made to ensure that your award is presented. To begin preparing for your internship, make certain that you accept the award and get in touch with me as soon as possible to talk about your availability and schedule. We wish you to be successful in the fashion world further and look forward to the moment when we can work together. Sincerely, Dirk Pelham Administrative Assistant Lilian Fung Collection, Inc. Part 3: Acceptance Letter Acceptance of the Choice Award Accepted - Rashana Develani Dear Ms. Fung, Your choice to make me a winner of the Lily Choice Award is something I am very appreciative of. I am thankful to be regarded as a great honor and feel grateful to the chance of being related to the Lilian Fung Collection. I would be happy to say that I will be present at the awards banquet on May 7 and I am looking forward to meeting your representative at the event. The six-month internship opportunity is something that I am especially excited about. I am free to engage in this engagement as soon as I am done with my studies, which would be at the end of my academic term in early June. I am mainly interested in modern women's casual clothes, textile designing, and detailing of their design, and also wish to gain some hands on experience in a working studio setting. I would also like to know more about the internship schedule, expectations, and any of the preparatory requirements. I am eager to join your team and make contributions to the Lilian Fung Collection.
